the interdecadal change of 30-yr SST normal in the 20th century is not monotonic, but it is generally characterized by a decrease in the 20-yr period from 1871–1890 to 1981–2000 in most of the world ocean, especially in the midlatitude North Atlantic, the midlatitude and subtropical North Pacific, and the tropical Indian Ocean.

the 30-tyr normals of SSTs are not stationary, especially in the tropical Indian and Pacific Oceans, but the interdecadal change is not monotonic, and there is a tendency for the 30- yr normal to become more stable.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interdecadal variations of 30-yr SST normals during 1871-2000 are significant in the tropical Indian ocean, the midlatitude north Pacific, the mid latitude north Atlantic, the mid latitude south Pacific and the south Indian ocean.
the 30- yr SST normals have undergone interdecadal changes since the late 1800s and the changes have been most significant during the past two decades.

the interdecadal variations in 30-yr SST normal are not negligible.
